contents.name: §6.1: the dictionary-order matrices m, A=(|S_λ∩C_ρ|) and B=CAᵀ, the Gram equation and the recursive triangular solve; Theorem 6.2 (reconstruction of the character table C=B(Aᵀ)⁻¹)
§6.3 Example: all A, B, C matrices for S₅, with the warning that the class columns are in the reverse of the usual order
§6.5 Corollary: det C is the product of all parts of all partitions of n, with the upper-triangular determinant proof
§18.2: definitions of hook, arm, leg, hook length and skew-hook (connected part of the rim removable to leave a diagram); §18.4 Lemma: natural bijection between hooks and skew-hooks
§19.2 Theorem (determinantal form [λ]=det([λ_i−i+j]), [m]=0 for m<0, [0] the multiplicative identity, products outer induction), with the expansion proofs of Examples 19.3–19.4
§21.3 Lemma: a product [μ][θ] of diagrams contains hook diagrams only in adjacent cancelling pairs, or none
contents.reason: James's auxiliary lemma serves his alternative orthogonality proof of the full-cycle value; the local proof of lem-character-value-on-a-full-cycle-is-supported-on-hooks evaluates the local determinantal form directly, so no scaffolded item consumes Lemma 21.3.

contents.name: §21.4 Theorem (full-cycle value: χ^λ(ρ)=(−1)^{n−x} exactly on the hooks λ=(x,1^{n−x}), 0 otherwise), with the column-orthogonality proof and normalisation at χ^{(n)}
§21.5 Lemma: c^λ_{ν,(x,1^{r−x})}=0 unless λ/ν is a union of m disjoint skew hooks with c columns, when it is binom(m−1,c−x); with the proof of the forced 1's and free spaces
§21.1 Theorem (the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule), proved from 21.4 and 21.5 plus Frobenius reciprocity and the exact alternating binomial cancellation
§21.2 Examples: χ^{(5,4,4)} equals −1 on (5,4,3,1) and 2 on (7,3,3), and is zero on classes containing an 8-, 9-, 10-, 11-, 12- or 13-cycle
§21.6 Corollary: if no hook length of λ is divisible by p then χ^λ vanishes on all p-singular elements, with the defect-zero remark |G|/deg χ^λ
§21.7 Theorem: for ν⊢n−r the signed sum of χ^λ over λ obtained from ν by an r-skew-hook vanishes off the classes containing an r-cycle, with the proof from 21.5 and 21.4
§21.8 Example (i): the four-term 3-cycle filter χ^{(6,2)}−χ^{(4,4)}−χ^{(3,2,2,1)}+χ^{(3,2,1,1,1)} of S₈ and its four legal 3-strips with heights 0,1,1,2
§21.8 Example (ii): the 2-cycle filter χ^{(n)}+χ^{(n−2,2)}−χ^{(n−2,1,1)} and the 2-modular and 3-modular block relations deduced from Examples 21.8 and 21.10
contents.reason: The 2-modular and 3-modular relations stated at the end of Example 21.8 are block-theoretic conclusions; their destination is the block page cores-quotients-and-blocks-of-symmetric-groups, and no ordinary character item on this pair consumes them.

contents.name: §21.10 Example: χ^{(n)}−χ^{(n−1,1)}+⋯±χ^{(m,m)} vanishes on classes containing an odd cycle, and the resulting 2-block statement
contents.reason: The example is a 2-cycle filter of the same shape as Theorem 21.7 together with a 2-block consequence; the filter itself is not needed because the pair's own filter proposition and its S₈ example are scaffolded, and the block statement belongs to the cores-and-blocks page.

contents.name: §21.9 and §21.11–21.14: relations on p-regular classes, the Nakayama conjecture for p-blocks and the modular classification programme
contents.reason: Nakayama's conjecture and the p-block classification are modular statements owned by the later cores-quotients-and-blocks-of-symmetric-groups page; this pair keeps the ordinary vanishing corollary and explicitly claims no block classification.

contents.name: §7 (7.1)–(7.2): the graded character ring R with the outer-product multiplication f·g=ind(f×g) and the characteristic map ch(f)=Σ f_ρ p_ρ/z_ρ
§7 (7.3): ch is an isometric isomorphism of R onto Λ, with the ring-homomorphism proof by Frobenius reciprocity and ch(η^n)=h_n
§7 (7.4)–(7.5): X^λ=det(η_{λ_i−i+j}) is a (virtual) character of S_n with ch(X^λ)=s_λ; an independent determinantal-form treatment
§7 (7.6)(i): the X^λ are exactly the irreducible characters of S_n
§7 (7.6)(ii): the degree f^λ is the number of standard tableaux of shape λ, i.e. n!/∏ h(λ)
§7 Example 3: restriction of χ^λ to S_m×S_n splits as Σ_{μ} χ^{λ/μ}×χ^μ (skew characters), with the Frobenius-reciprocity proof
§7 Example 5: the iterative combinatorial rule χ^λ_ρ=Σ_S(−1)^{ht(S)} over chains of border strips, credited to the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule
§7 Example 7: the closed formula for χ^λ at an element of type (r,1^{n−r}), obtained from the determinant of Example 6
contents.reason: The one-cycle closed formula is a specialisation of the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule to the classes (r,1^{n−r}); this pair proves the general recursive rule locally and scaffolds no separate item for that specialisation, so the formula is recorded but not built.

contents.name: §3 displayed expansion (2) with Example 11: s_μ p_r = Σ (−1)^{ht(λ−μ)} s_λ over border strips of length r, proved by the bialternant computation; with p_r=Σ_x(−1)^{r−x}s_{(x,1^{r−x})} this is the symmetric-function form of the alternating-hook cancellation
